summary: Customer runs an opaque, concentrated milk product through a processing line, currently samples it for fat and protein, and wants an initial in-line spectroscopy concept plus a practical comparison experiment to get earlier composition-change information, while keeping laboratory checks.

customer_premises.claim: A spectroscopy concept and a practical comparison experiment can be defined before the deciding facts (targets, ranges, interferences, installation point, accuracy, response time) are known.

customer_premises.claim: Laboratory checks will remain and are the appropriate fallback/reference.

unknowns: Which composition changes are of interest (e.g. which species/components, in addition to fat and protein).
Target concentration range and required resolution for fat and protein in the concentrated product.
Required accuracy of the in-line measurement versus the laboratory reference.
Texture/viscosity range and variability (impact on flow and on any optical window).
Installation point on the processing line and required measurement distance/probe geometry.
Cleaning regime, fouling behaviour and required maintenance interval for an in-line interface.
Matrix details: concentration level, particle/droplet size, scattering behaviour, interferences.
Laboratory reference method identity and its uncertainty.
Acceptance criteria for the comparison experiment (how success will be judged).
